title: Low-Level Design Engineer
blurb: Not one field but the rarest stack: someone who can read a disassembly, write a shader, tune a CUDA kernel and trace a memory exploit from one mental model. Three phases, no calendar. You move on when the quests are done.
core: Low-Level Design: systems, OS, databases, memory, networks
src: low_level_design_6yr_roadmap.html (the user's own roadmap file), years replaced by stages

tracks.name: Systems
tracks.desc: OS, architecture, memory, networks, databases, compilers

tracks.name: Security
tracks.desc: Exploit development, reverse engineering, cloud and kernel security

tracks.name: AI systems
tracks.desc: ML infrastructure, inference optimization, neural rendering

stages.name: Foundation
stages.blurb: The hardest stage, slow on purpose. C before C++, memory, architecture, OS, networks, databases, first exploits and first graphics math. This is where the moat is built.

topics.res: CS:APP chapters 1-6 with the labs; GDB, Valgrind
CS:APP; Nand2Tetris Part I; read x86-64 with objdump (read it, do not write it)
OSTEP (free at ostep.org); strace, ltrace
3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra (15 videos)
Python is the tool, C is the education
Effective Modern C++ (Scott Meyers); build a small allocator and a thread pool
Beej's Guide to Network Programming; Wireshark
CMU 15-445 (Andy Pavlo, YouTube); Database Internals by Alex Petrov, chapters 1-5
Hacking: The Art of Exploitation (Erickson); pwntools, pwndbg, ROPgadget
pwn.college (free); LiveOverflow on YouTube
Scratchapixel
learnopengl.com through Advanced Lighting

stages.name: Competitive depth
stages.blurb: Go deep in all tracks at once: Vulkan, web and cloud security, ML systems, LLVM, CUDA, OSCP, GSoC. Contribution-grade work and a portfolio that gets noticed.

topics.res: vulkan-tutorial.com; Brendan Galea's Vulkan Game Engine (YouTube); WebGPU is the cross-platform alternative
Burp Suite; OWASP
Karpathy micrograd and nanoGPT; fast.ai; Stanford CS231n
LLVM IR is the common language of shader compilers, ML compilers and security tools
HackTheBox, then the Pro Labs
Mesa 3D, LLVM, Rizin or Radare2, Wireshark; wgpu is a lower barrier
Most rejections are vague proposals
CUDA by Example (Sanders and Kandrot) with the NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide
OffSec PEN-200
TensorRT, ONNX Runtime
Physically Based Rendering (pbrt.org, free online)
Post it on a blog or arXiv; or a student track at USENIX Security, IEEE S&P or SIGGRAPH

stages.name: Cross-domain mastery
stages.blurb: Convergence. GPU security, neural rendering, kernel and hypervisor security, AI compilers. Publish, lead, then choose a role or graduate school.

topics.res: 3D Gaussian Splatting, instant-ngp
Triton (OpenAI), IREE; read the whole of tinygrad

milestones.t: Play picoCTF and solve about half the challenges
Advent of Code: first 10 days in C, the rest in Python
Finish CS:APP chapters 1-6 with the labs
Read OSTEP: virtualization, concurrency, persistence
Nand2Tetris Part I: build a computer from logic gates
Build a small allocator and a thread pool in C++
Build a toy key-value store in C++
Solve your first Easy HackTheBox machines
Play CSAW CTF with a team
Boss: render a 3D scene with your own software rasterizer, no graphics API
Get a first fix merged in a GSoC systems org (Mesa, LLVM, Rizin or Wireshark)
Submit a GSoC application with a detailed proposal
Complete one HackTheBox Pro Lab
Enter the DEF CON CTF qualifier
Compete in an ICPC regional
File a first bug bounty report on HackerOne or Bugcrowd
Build a tiny autograd engine (micrograd)
Publish one solid technical writeup or workshop paper
Apply for internships in security, graphics/GPU or AI systems
Boss: a complete deferred renderer built from scratch in C++
Compete in the DEF CON CTF main event
Present a poster at NVIDIA GTC
Get a student paper into IEEE S&P or USENIX Security
Land a CUDA kernel contribution in a real ML project
Maintain a small project or ship your own systems tool
Compete in Pwn2Own or Real World CTF
Decide: full-time role or graduate school
Boss: OSCP certified, with GSoC contributions, papers and a public GitHub that tells one story

calendar.t: DEF CON CTF qualifier; GSoC coding begins
CSAW CTF; USENIX Security deadline; internship applications open
ICPC regionals; Pwn2Own Toronto; IEEE S&P deadline
